Simulate Comb-BOIN12 Trials

Source: R/comb_boin12_simulate.R
comb_boin12_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of the Comb-BOIN12 design of Lu et al. (2025), the extension of BOIN12 to two drugs given together, which assigns each cohort to the most desirable combination by a utility that weighs the response against the DLT, and return the patients, DLTs and responses at every combination. This is the simulation engine behind sim_comb_boin12.

Usage

comb_boin12_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = c(1, 1),
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  n_star = 6,
  tie_break = c("higher", "random"),
  no_candidate = c("nearest", "stop"),
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, phi_T. It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a combination and of the MTD combination that bounds the OBD combination.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E, as in sim_boin12.

p_true

Numeric matrix. True DLT probability of every combination, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B.

p_resp

Numeric matrix of the same size. True response probability of every combination.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer vector of length 2. Levels of drug A and drug B of the first cohort. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. Number of patients at the current combination that ends the trial when the next cohort would stay there (see n_earlystop_rule). Defaults to NULL, which runs every trial to the maximum sample size, as in Lu et al. (2025).

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar. "with_stay" (the default) ends the trial at n_earlystop only when the next cohort would stay at the current combination; "simple" ends it in any case.

p_saf, p_tox

Numeric scalars or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic and lowest deemed overly toxic, which give the BOIN boundaries. Default to 0.6 * target and 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A combination is inadmissible, together with every combination with at least the same levels of both drugs, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A combination is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the cutoff cutoff_eli - offset to the lowest combination, as Lu et al. (2025) do with 0.85. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar. Amount by which cutoff_eli is lowered at the lowest combination when extrasafe is TRUE. Defaults to 0.05, as in sim_comb_boin; Lu et al. (2025) use 0.10.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both, as in sim_boin12. Default to 40 and 60. The utility pE - wT * pT of Lu et al. (2025) is psi00 = 100 * wT / (1 + wT) and psi11 = 100 / (1 + wT); their wT = 0.11 is psi00 = 9.90991 and psi11 = 90.09009.

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. Weight of the lowest acceptable utility in the utility benchmark, as in sim_boin12; it is the weight w_u of Lu et al. (2025), who use 0.6. Defaults to 0.5.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a combination divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_star

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current combination and a DLT rate between lambda_e and lambda_d, the next combination is chosen from the current one and the two below it. Defaults to 6.

tie_break

Character scalar. Choice among the combinations of equal desirability: "higher" (the default) keeps those with the highest sum of the two levels and draws one of them at random when several remain; "random" draws one of all the tied combinations. See Details.

no_candidate

Character scalar. What happens when none of the combinations allowed for the next cohort is admissible: "nearest" (the default) goes to the admissible combination nearest to the current one; "stop" ends the trial without an OBD combination. See Details.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type. Defaults to 0.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) or "binary", as in sim_boin12.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class comb_boin12_trials, which is a list with components

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp, n_tox_resp

Integer arrays with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B, of the patients treated, the DLTs, the responses and the patients with both a DLT and a response.

cohorts_used

Integer vector of the cohorts enrolled.

stop_reason

Character vector: "no_admissible_dose", "n_earlystop", "max_cohorts" or "no_admissible_candidate" (only with no_candidate = "stop").

early_stop

Logical vector, TRUE for the trials stopped because no combination was admissible or, with no_candidate = "stop", because no combination allowed for the next cohort was admissible. These trials select no OBD combination.

design

"Comb-BOIN12".

boundary

List with lambda_e, lambda_d, u_low and u_benchmark.

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

After each cohort, with phat the DLT rate at the current combination (j, k): the trial stops when no combination is admissible; when phat is at least lambda_d, the next combination is the most desirable of the admissible combinations below (j, k), that is with levels at most j and k, that have the highest sum of the two levels: (j - 1, k) or (j, k - 1) when either is admissible, as in Lu et al. (2025), and lower ones otherwise; the current one when there is none. When phat is above lambda_e and at least n_star patients have been treated, the next combination is the most desirable of (j, k), (j - 1, k) and (j, k - 1); otherwise of (j, k) and its four neighbors (j - 1, k), (j, k - 1), (j + 1, k) and (j, k + 1). Only admissible combinations inside the matrix are considered. When none of these is admissible, the admissible combination nearest to the current one (by the sum of the differences of the two levels) is chosen, then the one with the lowest sum of the levels, then the most desirable. The desirability is that of BOIN12 (boin12_decision_table). Untried combinations have a DLT rate of 0 and are admissible unless excluded by the DLT data of a lower combination.

With no_candidate = "stop", the trial stops instead, without an OBD combination and with the stopping reason "no_admissible_candidate", when none of these combinations is admissible and when phat is at least lambda_d and no combination below the current one is admissible. At the lowest combination, a phat of at least lambda_d still keeps the next cohort there when it is admissible.

Lu et al. (2025) do not state how ties of desirability are broken nor what happens when no candidate is admissible. With tie_break = "higher", among tied combinations those with the highest sum of the levels are kept, so that the design escalates when an untried combination is as desirable as the current one, and a tie that remains (between (j + 1, k) and (j, k + 1), for example) is broken at random. The allocation percentages published by Lu et al. (2025) agree with this rule, and not with a random choice among all the tied combinations nor with a fixed preference for one drug (see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Lu2025.R). The two settings of no_candidate could not be told apart from the published results. With one row or one column, the trials are those of boin12_simulate without its exploration rule; Lu et al. (2025) have no such rule.

When psi00 + psi11 is 100, as for the utility of Lu et al. (2025), the desirability does not depend on the number of patients with both a DLT and a response, and combinations with the same numbers of patients, DLTs and responses tie exactly, whatever the rounding of psi00 and psi11.

Each patient draws two uniform variates in enrollment order, the first for the DLT and the second for the response. A decision between tied combinations draws one more variate when a tie remains after the rule of tie_break.

References

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276. doi:10.1080/19466315.2024.2370403

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

See also

sim_comb_boin12, comb_boin12_select_obd, boin12_simulate

Examples

# Scenario 16 of Lu et al. (2025), with their utility (wT = 0.11)
p_true <- matrix(c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.15, 0.20, 0.45), nrow = 2)
p_resp <- matrix(c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60), nrow = 2)
trials <- comb_boin12_simulate(
  target = 0.33, target_resp = 0.2, p_true = p_true, p_resp = p_resp,
  n_cohort = 14, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200,
  psi00 = 100 * 0.11 / 1.11, psi11 = 100 / 1.11, benchmark_weight = 0.6,
  extrasafe = TRUE, offset = 0.10, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated Comb-BOIN12 trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   dose levels          : 2 of drug A, 3 of drug B
#>   DLT limit            : 0.33
#>   response limit       : 0.2
#>   cohorts              : 14 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 42
#> 
#> Patients treated, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2    B3
#> A1 4.16 5.62 12.09
#> A2 3.52 8.23  7.98
#> 
#> DLTs observed, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 0.16 0.88 2.50
#> A2 0.32 1.30 3.56
#> 
#> Responses observed, average per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 0.45 1.68 6.18
#> A2 0.68 3.18 4.76
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#>        max_cohorts no_admissible_dose 
#>                 99                  1
